25–35 days
From sowing; timing depends on the variety and growing conditions.
Sow directly in a pot or bed. Briefly soak hard-coated seeds if needed, then plant shallowly.
A bright spot with about 4–6 hours of direct sunlight each day.
Use a loose, organic-rich growing medium in a container with drainage holes.
Keep the medium moist. Check its surface daily and water when it begins to dry.
Mix in mature compost before planting. If you add fertilizer, follow the product label.
Thin seedlings so they are not overcrowded.
Harvest the leafy tips once the plant is bushy; leave nodes so it can regrow.
Holes in leaves: check for caterpillars and snails in the morning or evening.
Pale leaves: check light, moisture, and the growing medium before adding fertilizer.
This harvest range is a starting estimate. Check the seed packet for the variety you are growing.
25–40 days
From sowing; young leaves may be ready sooner.
Scatter seeds thinly where they will grow. Cover with a very light layer of medium.
Morning sun or a bright spot with about 4–6 hours of direct light.
Use a fine, loose medium enriched with mature compost and good drainage.
Water gently so seeds stay in place. Keep the medium moist while seeds germinate.
Mature compost is often enough at first. Avoid over-fertilizing leafy vegetables.
Thin seedlings after they emerge to give each plant room.
Pick outer leaves or harvest the whole plant when it reaches a useful size.
Seedlings falling over: reduce standing water and improve airflow.
Holes or curled leaves: check the undersides for small pests.
Growth speed depends on variety, temperature, and light.
30–50 days
From sowing or planting; check the seed packet for its starting point.
Start in a seed tray and transplant after several true leaves appear, or sow directly in the final container.
Bright light and morning sun. Protect the plant from long periods of intense heat.
Use a fertile, loose medium that holds moisture without becoming waterlogged.
Water evenly when the top layer begins to dry. Avoid large swings in moisture.
Use mature compost as a base. Follow the fertilizer label and observe the plant before adding more.
Transplant carefully to avoid disturbing the roots.
Remove old leaves and give plants enough space for airflow.
Holes in leaves: check for caterpillars and small beetles.
Early flowering: heat and water stress can make a plant flower sooner.
Harvest time varies by variety and whether the count starts at sowing or transplanting.
50–75 days
Usually counted from planting; variety and planting method affect timing.
Sow directly in the final container, or start in a pot that can be moved without disturbing the roots.
Choose a spot with around 6 or more hours of direct sun when possible.
Use a deep, fertile medium with mature compost and good drainage.
Keep moisture steady, especially during flowering and fruiting. Water at the base.
Mix in compost before planting. Follow the fertilizer label for any extra feeding.
Set up a sturdy stake or trellis while the plant is young.
Harvest regularly when fruits reach the size expected for the variety.
Powdery or spotted leaves: inspect symptoms closely and avoid wetting leaves excessively.
Flowers dropping: review heat, watering, pollination, and overall plant health.
Cucumbers need room to climb. Match this estimate to the local variety you choose.
45–70 days
From sowing; harvest may continue over several weeks.
Sow seeds directly beside a sturdy stake or trellis.
A sunny spot with around 6 or more hours of direct sunlight.
Use a loose medium that drains well, in a sufficiently deep container.
Water at the base when the medium begins to dry. Keep moisture steady during flowering.
Add mature compost before planting. Avoid extra nitrogen unless the plant shows a need.
Guide the vine onto its trellis as it begins to climb.
Pick young pods regularly to encourage more harvests.
Yellow or curled leaves: check the undersides for small pests.
Few pods: check light, moisture, and whether flowers are setting.
Variety and local conditions affect when harvest begins.
70–90 days
Often counted from transplanting; starting from seed takes longer.
Start in a seed tray, then move a sturdy seedling into a large pot after it has adjusted.
Choose a place with around 6–8 hours of direct sun when possible.
Use a loose potting medium rich in compost that drains excess water quickly.
Water regularly at the base and keep moisture fairly steady while fruiting.
Use compost when preparing the medium. Follow the fertilizer label and plant stage for extra feeding.
Add a support when the plant begins to grow tall.
Remove leaves touching the medium and inspect the plant regularly.
Leaf spots: photograph both the upper and lower leaf surfaces for a closer check.
Cracked fruit: changing moisture may contribute; aim for more consistent watering.
Reaching 90 days depends on an early variety and the count start date. Check the seed packet.
